walkthroughs.body_html:
Algorithm Design & Problem Solving — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Algorithm Design & Problem Solving brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Algorithm Design & Problem Solving.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which technique involves breaking a problem into smaller sub-problems?
options: Abstraction
Decomposition
Iteration
Encapsulation

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of a trace table?
options: To compile code
To track variable values during execution
To draw a flowchart
To store program output

mcqs.q: Why must a recursive function have a base case?
options: Because the syntax requires it.
To make the function run faster.
Without it, the function calls itself indefinitely, causing a stack overflow.

mcqs.q: How many layers are in the OSI model?
options: It is impossible to break.
7 (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application).
4 (confusing with TCP/IP model).

mcqs.q: What is the main advantage of asymmetric encryption?
options: Secure key exchange without sharing a secret in advance.
It is impossible to break.
It is faster than symmetric encryption.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Pseudocode”?
options: Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Abstraction”?
options: A finite, ordered sequence of unambiguous steps that solves a problem or completes a task.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
Structured English-like description of an algorithm, independent of any programming language.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Trace table”?
options: Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
Removing unnecessary detail from a problem to focus on the essential features.
Table used to track the changing values of variables as an algorithm executes step by step.
Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.

options: Diagram using standardised shapes (oval, rectangle, diamond) to represent the flow of an algorithm.
Breaking a complex problem into smaller, more manageable sub-problems.
